Farmland in this area should be on slopes of less than 8% to prevent excessive erosion.
As shown in exhibit 15 of the Westmoreland Resources Mining Plan the reclaimed area will be much leveler than now exists. This would offer an opportunity for farming more land than is now being farmed. Wildlife and Fish
Adverse impacts on wildlife species will be mitigated primarily by providing habitat diversity in reclaimed areas through the planting of trees and shrubs. Wildlife population responses to mining and reclamation are monitored in a continuous program by Westmoreland Resources. A study is in progress to determine responses of sharptail grouse to the mining of dancing grounds, and to develop methods of re-establishing dancing grounds on reclaimed areas.
Associated mining facilities, such as powerlines and fences will be constructed so as to minimize hazards to wildlife species.
Downstream aquatic habitats will be protected from pollution by water control facilities. Construction of sediment ponds may provide limited aquatic habitat; water quality in the existing sediment pond has been consistently good. If suitable aquatic habitats are created, appropriate fish species will be introduced and where possible, impoundments will be managed to provide waterfowl habitat.
